question: If we could see what an AI is quietly thinking, would that make us trust it more or less?
reflection: Looking inside our tools, not only at their answers, is how trust can be earned instead of assumed.

sources.subject: Anthropic's J-space exposes Claude's hidden reasoning layer

one_line: Anthropic says it found a small hidden workspace inside Claude where its silent reasoning happens, opening a new way to check what a model is planning.

top_stories.title: A hidden scratchpad inside Claude
top_stories.what: Anthropic reports a small internal space, which it calls the J-space, that holds what Claude is actively working on; removing it reportedly breaks multi-step reasoning, and it showed warning signs in a model trained to sabotage code.
top_stories.why: Tools that reveal hidden intentions could become part of how organisations audit AI systems before trusting them with sensitive work.

top_stories.title: A free AI security tester
top_stories.what: An open-source framework called T3MP3ST turns coding agents into automated security testers and reportedly scored about 90% on a public hacking benchmark, with risky tools held behind human approval.
top_stories.why: Cheaper security testing helps smaller organisations, but the same tools lower the barrier for attackers.

top_stories.title: A large free library of agent skills
top_stories.what: A developer published his full collection of reusable agent skills for research, documentation and coordinating several agents.
top_stories.why: Ready-made skills show how a team's know-how can be packaged so AI assistants follow the same methods every time.

top_stories.title: A world model that keeps learning after release
top_stories.what: NYU researchers describe a model that keeps adapting at test time to correct its own mistakes.
top_stories.why: Models that change after deployment need new kinds of monitoring, a point to raise in AI governance work.

saudi_lens.text: Better ways to inspect model reasoning support the trust and transparency principles in Saudi AI ethics guidance for public-sector use.

idea.title: Team skills library
idea.pitch: Turn the team's standard research methods, such as interview coding or literature screening, into written skill files an AI assistant can follow.
idea.first_step: Write one skill file for a task the team repeats often and test it on two past projects.

idea_kids.title: Think aloud game
idea_kids.pitch: Children solve a simple puzzle in pairs while one says every thought out loud and the other draws the steps, to learn how thinking can be made visible.
idea_kids.first_step: Choose five short puzzles and make a simple drawing sheet with numbered boxes for each step.
